tasks.title: T15-US-001: Ratify the shared canonical schema contract
tasks.description:
As an architect, I need a single canonical node/edge schema both projects target so entities and relationships mean the same thing everywhere.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- Author docs/canonical-schema.md defining node types (language, language-family, writing-system, culture, archaeological-culture, urheimat-hypothesis, religion, deity, myth-motif, art-tradition, literary-tradition, cuisine, ingredient, trade-good, battle, place, migration-route) and edge types (descended-from, split-from, merged-with, influenced-by, conquered-by, absorbed-into, spoken-in, located-in, contemporary-with, part-of-period, borrowed-from, cognate-with, derived-from, syncretized-with)
- Define the identity scheme: csid primary; anchors wikidata_qid, iso639_3/glottocode (languages), pleiades_id/tgn_id (places); LinguaScrape id retained as an alias column
- Define mandatory provenance columns (source, source_url, retrieved_at, confidence) matching culture-scrape's data model
- Emit a machine-readable schema (JSON or YAML) checked into shared/ so both repos can validate against it
- Type checks pass (`npm run check`)

Project context: LinguaScrape is a TypeScript/React/Vite + Express app with TSV-first storage (lexicons/*.tsv, 57 files), served by server/index.ts + server/routes.ts, client in client/src. culture-scrape (vendored in-repo at packages/culture-scrape/) is a Python CLI/FastAPI engine that emits a canonical node/edge graph and exports to Neo4j + Datalog. The agreed data-layer target is a SHARED CANONICAL SCHEMA with Neo4j/Datalog as the correlation system-of-record; TSV stays the portable source of truth; the app backend stays TypeScript (no Python rewrite). The authoritative design is docs/culturescrape-integration.md. tasks.description:

- Ambiguous candidates are listed with their competing matches and confidence; never auto-merged silently
- vitest tests cover key emission and the ambiguity report on fixtures
- Document how to feed this into culture-scrape's reconcile step under packages/culture-scrape/ (same repo)

tasks.title: T15-US-007: Bidirectional TSV write-back path
tasks.description:

- Add a documented round-trip: LinguaScrape contribution-system edits export to canonical TSV; culture-scrape derived/enriched facts import back into lexicons where a canonical->lexicon mapping exists
- Write-back never overwrites human-curated values without an explicit flag; provenance columns are preserved
- A round-trip vitest test asserts export->import produces no data loss on fixtures
- Conflicts (same field, different source) are reported, not silently resolved
- Document the sync cadence and ownership (which side is authoritative per field)
